newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean stocks end week active and firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean stocks end week active and firmer.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks ended the week on Friday active and firmer, largely boosted by positive local investor sentiment, brokers said.
"Now the market is being largely driven by local buyers; the foreigners are selling. They've done very well and are profit-taking on some of their stocks," one broker said.
Zimbabwe's key 57-counter industrial index added on 93.77 points to close at 10,112.80 on Friday, but lost 178.71 points on the week.

Friday's winners included agricultural investors Chemco, which surged 400 cents to 4,000 while cement producer Porthold at 1,700, and bankers FMB and Barclays at 5,800 and 3,400 respectively all added 100 cents.

National Foods went up 70 cents to 700, Zimbabwe Newspapers put on 50 cents to 2,950 and Zimbabwe Alloys, wood and glass product manufacturers PGI, teaand coffee growers Tanganda and retailers Tedco all went up 10 cents to 790, 610, 360, and 1,170.

Against the trend, tobacco firm Rothmans shed 100 cents to 6,000, steel door and window maker Radar lost 25 cents to 475, tyre company NTS eased 20 cents to 530 and another tea and coffee producer, EHPL went down 130, while 10 cent losses were recorded in battery firm Chloride at 140, haulage company Clan at 520, and seed group SeedCo at 230.

Minings were also firmer in active trade, with gains in gold company Falcon Warrants, which rose 10 cents to 40 and nickel producer Bindura which added 40 cents to 850 helping nudge the seven-counter index 7.05 points up to 1,054.49. This was, however, a 61.81 point loss on the week.
